story.head: Who drives the play: the Senators
paras: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Senators have won three straight, and the Flyers (7-11-6) beat Buffalo 4-3 on Tuesday. Going in, the Flyers are sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Sens second in the Atlantic (tied for fourth).
The Flyers’ record (.417) is about what their chances are worth. The Senators’ record (.682) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.595), largely because they’re 7-2 in one-goal games.

The Flyers take away shots from the point (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). Philadelphia has scored 2.38 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. On the other side, the Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and get into more chippy games than almost anyone (3rd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Matvei Michkov (11 G / 8 A / 19 P in 24 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Trevor Zegras (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 24 GP) is next in line. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (11 G / 15 A / 26 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven goals in eleven games against Philadelphia since 2023-24. Drake Batherson (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 22 GP) is next in line.

Joseph Woll (4-6-2 / .898 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to start for Philadelphia, and Samuel Ersson (3-3-2 / .884 SV% in 7 GS) for Ottawa. Woll has a .874 save percentage in seven starts against the Senators, well under his usual .905. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Senators usually control more of the chances than the Flyers do.

items.text: The Senators are newly without Carter Yakemchuk, and have been without Warren Foegele, Jonas Johansson and William Eklund for several games. Samuel Ersson is expected to start.
Matvei Michkov has eleven goals on chances worth about 6.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Trevor Zegras is two goals from 100.
Joseph Woll has never won in Ottawa: he is 0-3-0 there in his career.
